name: Marina Operations and Maintenance Fund

established.purpose: To receive a $1.8M State Division of Boating and Waterways loan to build the Waterfront; berth and lease revenue was expected to cover debt service, maintenance and operations of the entire Waterfront.

legal_basis: Enterprise fund; four State DBW loans (1964 $1.8M, 1971 $1.5M, 1985 $2.0M, 2001 $7.8M authorized, $7.1M drawn); Council budget and AAO actions
scope: 1.8 miles of streets, 11 parking lots, 5 miles of pathways, three parks (Cesar Chavez, Shorebird, Horseshoe), 1,000 berths, public docks and launch ramp, dry storage, office building, 125-127 University, corp yard, 199 Seawall, restrooms, Shorebird Nature Center, Adventure Playground, hotel and restaurant sites, 13 leases and licenses, all utilities

annual.note: Government-wide ten-year schedule: charges for services vs expenses
Revenue includes ARPA-era support recorded as charges; see flows

Proprietary fund statement: operating revenue $6,925,076 (berths $4,608,077; leases $2,274,799); operating loss $401,892; investment earnings $271,251 less interest $261,218; change in net position -$415,968

Proprietary fund statement: operating revenue $7,594,812 (berths $5,329,258; leases $2,265,554); operating loss $5,979,084; State capital grant $7,689,069; interfund loan receipt $2,477,099 (financing, not revenue); change in net position +$1,565,243 after a -$63,380 restatement
Staff 'actual' as of Sept 2026, cash basis. Revenue includes the $1.4M General Fund subsidy. Ending balance is staff's cash balance, not audited net position
Staff forecast; assumes no Doubletree rent and no parking revenue

flows.stated_reason: Demolition and replacement of wooden docks and piles; new utilities; barrier-free docks; restroom replacement
flows.terms: 4.50%, payable August 1 each year, $485,719/yr, final payment FY2041; $9.0M authorized, $7.1M drawn; balance $5,640,491 at 6/30/2024 and $5,415,120 at 6/30/2025

flows.note: Staff deck figure; the ACFR does not break ARPA out by receiving fund

flows.stated_reason: D and E dock replacement ($8.26M project) in place of a State DBW loan that would have cost ~$4.5M in interest over 30 years
flows.terms: Repaid from the total Transient Occupancy Tax generated in the Waterfront starting FY2025 until paid off, plus a one-time $500,000 interest payment from TOT. Staff estimated the General Fund loses $1.0-1.5M/yr of TOT revenue until repayment is complete.
flows.note: The May 2025 staff deck lists '$5.5M from Workers Comp fund for capital projects' under FY24. The FY2024 ACFR records no interfund loan receipt by the Marina Operations fund and no amount due from it at June 30, 2024. The FY2025 ACFR records a $2,477,099 interfund loan receipt, shown as due to the General Fund. How the $5.5M was booked is an open question (see status).
Receiving funds not named in the deck

flows.from_fund: City central services / Workers' Compensation Fund
flows.stated_reason: Reduced indirect cost charges and a Workers' Compensation contribution holiday
flows.note: Split between the indirect reduction and the holiday not given
Staff decks reference a $15M State earmark; $7.69M is the amount recognized in FY2025

flows.instrument: ACFR FY2025, statement of cash flows and Note: Due To/From Other Funds
flows.terms: Recorded as due to the General Fund at June 30, 2025; no repayment terms disclosed
flows.note: May be a draw against the 2023 $5.5M authorization; the ACFR names the General Fund, not the Workers' Compensation Fund, as the lender

flows.stated_reason: Address ~$700K revenue loss: fund balance exhausted; South Cove East Dock repair unfunded; security cut 50%; marketing cut; all hourly staff cut; career staff hours shifted to nights and weekends

flows.instrument: Measure Y (Nov 2024); Council Resolution Clarifying the Intent of Measure Y, Sept 24, 2024, Item 10
flows.stated_reason: Park and landscape maintenance in the Waterfront including Cesar Chavez Park moved from the Marina Fund to the Parks Tax
flows.terms: The ballot question named parks, trees and landscaping generally; the Council's pre-election resolution stated the intent to cover Waterfront park and landscape maintenance. Staff: this shift alone covered the fund's $1.1M structural deficit plus $200K cost growth and $200K revenue decline.

flows.stated_reason: Transfer to Marina Fund to offset projected deficit
flows.terms: Funded by redirecting about $2.5M of Measure U1 revenue from the Small Sites housing program to General Fund and Marina Fund costs. Staff report: 'not sustainable long-term solutions.'

flows.stated_reason: Council Recommendation: FY25 GF savings to support Marina Fund deficit ($74,626 + $126,374 + $25,000)
flows.note: The same AAO carries 'Transfer to Marina Fund from General Fund 1,409,886' as the FY2026 total

flows.from_fund: City central services / Workers' Compensation Fund
flows.stated_reason: Reduced indirect costs and Workers' Compensation holiday

flows.instrument: Council, June 2025 (parking fees in three Waterfront lots; Adventure Playground entry fee)
flows.terms: Parking budgeted $150K (FY27) / $185K (FY28); playground $75K / $100K. BCDC rejected the parking permit; a major permit is now required. Playground fee gate not installed until Oct 2026; FY27 projection cut to $40K.
flows.note: Budgeted amount; staff now expects most of it not to arrive in FY27

flows.stated_reason: Slip rental, liveaboard, electricity surcharge, parking pass and launch ramp increases (~$250K/yr); recreation program fee increases (~$100K/yr)

Waterfront Manager to 85%, Assistant Civil Engineer to 60%, 5% of Deputy Director shifted to Parks Tax, minor maintenance -$100K, security/marketing/supplies -$81K; net of a Senior Marina Assistant added

flows.instrument: Lease (60-year term to 2080; base rent ~$82K/month plus percentage rent)
flows.stated_reason: Hotel stopped paying regular rent in early 2025 (Jan per May 2025 deck; March per Sept 2026 deck); paid $964,680 in Sept 2025; nothing since Dec 2025; ~$890K owed as of Sept 2026 (9 months base rent, 3 quarters percentage rent)
flows.terms: Not written off; recorded here as revenue at risk. Budget assumed 35% of rent for FY27-28; actual zero. Staff: potential loss $840K through FY28.

obligations.note: Failing docks and pilings; no capital reserve
Inner harbor/docks $33.4M; parking lots $17.3M; streets $15.7M; shorelines/pathways/pier $55.4M; dredging and seawall $20.2M; City buildings $10.8M
Due to the General Fund; terms not disclosed
Authorized from the Workers' Compensation Fund; repayable from Waterfront TOT plus $500K; how much has been drawn and repaid is not disclosed in either ACFR

open_questions: How the $5.5M Workers' Compensation loan authorized July 25, 2023 was booked: the FY2024 ACFR shows no interfund loan to the Marina fund; the FY2025 ACFR shows $2,477,099 due to the General Fund.
Whether Waterfront TOT has been diverted to repay the loan since FY2025, and how much; staff decks describe FY25 and FY26 'Workers' Compensation holidays' instead.
Which 'other funds' absorbed the FY2024 $800K cost shift.
Whether the FY2025 $11.13M 'charges for services' in the government-wide schedule includes the interfund loan; the proprietary statement shows $7.59M operating revenue.

The FY2025 ACFR ten-year schedule repeats FY2022-level figures under 2023 and 2024 and shifts earlier years by two columns, for every business-type row; the FY2024 ACFR's schedule does not. Which is correct for 2021-2024 should be confirmed with Finance; this file uses the FY2024 ACFR for FY2015-2024.
